meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first: who decided that, and before or after anyone spoke to him?
You can skip the pleasantries, Hale. I asked you a question, and I'm still waiting for the answer.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero on Owen's essay to be withdrawn, an apology, and an explanation of who decided it and whether Owen was heard before it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing and still wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology and an explanation; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended before anyone got near it.
What moved her: Nothing, because no evidence or ownership of the process was offered before the meeting ended.
What cost ground: Hale answered her direct question about who decided the zero with a polite thank-you, which to a litigator reads as dodging and made her press harder.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's evidence never came near that night because no evidence was shown; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asks who decided the zero and whether Owen was heard first, answer it straight away by owning in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called home, then put a dated document in front of her.
